paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples.
model_annotation: This line chart compares the performance of two example selection strategies—ST-ES (blue line with circular markers) and Random (orange line with circular markers)—as measured by minADE₂₀ (in units of length, ranging from 0.13 to 0.14) across varying numbers of in-context examples, displayed on the x-axis which ranges from 0 to 8 with integer tick labels. The y-axis, labeled “minADE₂₀ (←)”, uses a linear scale from 0.13 to 0.14. The ST-ES line begins at 0.140 and ends at approximately 0.134, showing a general downward trend with fluctuations, including a dip to 0.130 at x=2 and a minimum at x=4 (0.130). The Random line begins at 0.140 and ends at approximately 0.139, remaining relatively flat between x=0 and x=2, then rising to a peak of 0.139 at x=8, with a dip to 0.130 at x=6.

model_annotations.English: This line plot compares the performance of two example selection strategies—ST-ES and Random—as measured by minADE₂₀ (in units of distance) across varying numbers of in-context examples, ranging from 0 to 8. The x-axis, labeled "Number of Examples," uses a linear scale with integer tick marks at intervals of 2, spanning from 0 to 8. The y-axis, labeled "minADE₂₀ (←)", uses a linear scale with tick marks at intervals of 0.001, ranging from 0.13 to 0.14. The ST-ES strategy is represented by a blue line with circular markers and a solid line, starting at approximately 0.141 and showing a general downward trend to a minimum of 0.130 at 4 examples, before rising slightly to 0.133 at 8 examples. The Random strategy is represented by an orange line with circular markers and a solid line, starting at approximately 0.141, dropping to 0.131 at 2 examples, remaining relatively flat around 0.131 until 6 examples, then rising to approximately 0.140 at 8 examples.
